arxiv-2103-07755.title: Graded ideals of König type Thanks: The second author was supported by JSPS KAKENHI 19H00637.
arxiv-2103-07755.creator: Jürgen Herzog, Takayuki Hibi and Somayeh Moradi
arxiv-2103-07755.description: Abstract . Inspired by the notion of König graphs we introduce graded ideals of König type with respect to a monomial order < < . It is shown that if I I is of König type, then the Cohen–Macaulay property of in < ⁡ ( I ) \operatorname{in}_{<}(I) does not depend on the characteristic of the base field.

arxiv-2106-14444.title: A Knowledge-Grounded Dialog System Based on Pre-Trained Language Models
arxiv-2106-14444.creator: Weijie Zhang, Jiaoxuan Chen, Haipang Wu, Sanhui Wan, Gongfeng Li
arxiv-2106-14444.description: Abstract We present a knowledge-grounded dialog system developed for the ninth Dialog System Technology Challenge (DSTC9) Track 1 - Beyond Domain APIs: Task-oriented Conversational Modeling with Unstructured Knowledge Access . We leverage transfer learning with existing language models to accomplish the tasks in this challenge track.

arxiv-2112-11480.title: On the Compression of Natural Language Models
arxiv-2112-11480.creator: Saeed Damadi
arxiv-2112-11480.description: Abstract Deep neural networks are effective feature extractors but they are prohibitively large for deployment scenarios. Due to the huge number of parameters, interpretability of parameters in different layers is not straight-forward. This is why neural networks are sometimes considered black boxes. Although simpler models are easier to explain, finding them is not easy.

arxiv-2201-11256.title: Structural sensitivity in the functional responses of predator-prey models
arxiv-2201-11256.creator: Sarah K. Wyse, Maria M. Martignoni, May Anne Mata, Eric Foxall, Rebecca C. Tyson
arxiv-2201-11256.description: Abstract In mathematical modeling, several different functional forms can often be used to fit a data set equally well, especially if the data is sparse. In such cases, these mathematically different but similar looking functional forms are typically considered interchangeable.

arxiv-2208-03067.title: Large vocabulary speech recognition for languages of Africa: multilingual modeling and self-supervised learning
arxiv-2208-03067.creator: Sandy Ritchie, You-Chi Cheng, Mingqing Chen
arxiv-2208-03067.description: Abstract Almost none of the 2,000+ languages spoken in Africa have widely available automatic speech recognition systems, and the required data is also only available for a few languages. We have experimented with two techniques which may provide pathways to large vocabulary speech recognition for African languages: multilingual modeling and self-supervised learning.

arxiv-2309-02460.title: Effective Illicit Account Detection on Large Cryptocurrency MultiGraphs DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; October 21 –- 25, 2024; Boise, Idaho, USA ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/18/06
arxiv-2309-02460.creator: Zhihao Ding, Jieming Shi, Qing Li, Jiannong Cao
arxiv-2309-02460.description: Abstract . Cryptocurrencies are rapidly expanding and becoming vital in digital financial markets. However, the rise in cryptocurrency-related illicit activities has led to significant losses for users. To protect the security of these platforms, it is critical to identify illicit accounts effectively.

arxiv-2310-14425.title: Reformulation of the Stable Adams Conjecture Thanks: ∗ partially supported by the Simons Foundation
arxiv-2310-14425.creator: Eric M. Friedlander ∗
arxiv-2310-14425.description: Abstract . We revisit methods of proof of the Adams Conjecture in order to correct and supplement earlier efforts to prove analogous conjectures in the stable homotopy category. We utilize simplicial schemes over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic and a rigid version of Artin-Mazur étale homotopy theory.

arxiv-2404-12100.title: Rationally independent free fermions with local hopping
arxiv-2404-12100.creator: Jonathon Riddell, Bruno Bertini
arxiv-2404-12100.description: Abstract Rationally independent free fermions are those where sums of single-particle energies multiplied by arbitrary rational coefficients vanish only if the coefficients are all zero. This property guaranties that they have no degeneracies in the many-body spectrum and gives them relaxation properties more similar to those of generic systems.

arxiv-2411-13053.title: MEGL: Multimodal Explanation-Guided Learning
arxiv-2411-13053.creator: Yifei Zhang, Tianxu Jiang, Bo Pan, Jingyu Wang, Guangji Bai, Liang Zhao
arxiv-2411-13053.description: Abstract Explaining the decision-making processes of Artificial Intelligence (AI) models is crucial for addressing their “black box” nature, particularly in tasks like image classification. Traditional eXplainable AI (XAI) methods typically rely on unimodal explanations, either visual or textual, each with inherent limitations. Visual explanations highlight key regions but often lack rationale, while textual explanations provide context without spatial grounding.

arxiv-2502-20951.title: Linear magnetoresistance, anomalous Hall effect and de Haas-van Alphen oscillations in antiferromagnetic SmAg 2 Ge 2 single crystals
arxiv-2502-20951.creator: Kanchan Bala, Rahul Verma, Shovan Dan, Suman Nandi, Ruta Kulkarni, Bahadur Singh, A. Thamizhavel
arxiv-2502-20951.description: Abstract Understanding the interplay among magnetism, electron correlations, and complex electronic structures in rare-earth materials requires both high-quality single crystals and systematic investigation of their electronic properties. In this study, we have successfully grown a single crystal of SmAg 2 Ge 2 and investigated its anisotropic physical properties and de Haas-van Alphen (dHvA) quantum oscillations through experimental and theoretical approaches.

arxiv-2504-20070.title: Improving Deep Knowledge Tracing via Gated Architectures and Adaptive Optimization
arxiv-2504-20070.creator: Altun Shukurlu
arxiv-2504-20070.description: Abstract Deep Knowledge Tracing (DKT) [ 1 ] models student learning behavior by leveraging Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) to predict future performance based on historical interaction data. However, the original implementation relied on standard RNNs in the Lua-based Torch framework, limiting extensibility and reproducibility. In this paper, we revisit the DKT model from two perspectives: architectural improvements and optimization efficiency.

arxiv-2507-09753.title: Do we need equivariant models for molecule generation?
arxiv-2507-09753.creator: Ewa M. Nowara, Joshua Rackers, Patricia Suriana, Pan Kessel, Max Shen, Andrew Martin Watkins, Michael Maser
arxiv-2507-09753.description: Abstract Deep generative models are increasingly used for molecular discovery, with most recent approaches relying on equivariant graph neural networks (GNNs) under the assumption that explicit equivariance is essential for generating high-quality 3D molecules. However, these models are complex, difficult to train, and scale poorly.

arxiv-2601-07655.title: To report or not to report: Optimal claim reporting in a bonus-malus system
arxiv-2601-07655.creator: Lea Enzi and Stefan Thonhauser
arxiv-2601-07655.description: Abstract Abstract We study an optimal claim reporting problem in a bonus-malus setting. We assume, that the insurance contract consists of two regimes, where reporting a claim leads to a transition to a higher-premium regime, whereas remaining claim-free for a prespecified time period results in a shift to the lower premium regime.

britannica-1911-tuscany.title: Tuscany (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-tuscany.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-tuscany.description: Article 'Tuscany' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. of the western part of the centre of the peninsula, bounded N.W. by Liguria and Emilia, E. by the Marches and Umbria, S.E. by the province of Rome and W. by the Mediterranean. It consists of eight provinces, Arezzo, Firenze (Florence), Grosseto, Livorno (Leghorn), Lucca, Massa-Carrara, Pisa and Siena, and has an area of 9304 sq.

plos-pone-0354275.title: Dopaminergic genetic variation and response to social comparative feedback when learning a motor sequence task
plos-pone-0354275.creator: Allison F Lewis, Rachel Bohnenkamp, Jill Campbell Stewart
plos-pone-0354275.description: Dopaminergic genetic variation and response to social comparative feedback when learning a motor sequence task

pmc-10571412.title: Breaking ground: nursing-led approach to alleviating constipation in Parkinson’s disease
pmc-10571412.creator: Wenyao Geng, Mengdie Ren, Feng Zhao, Fuguo Yang, Heng Liu
pmc-10571412.description: BackgroundConstipation is one of the most common non-motor symptoms in PD patients, and the constipation, can appear before motor symptoms. Incorrect treatment of constipation in PD patients can result in colonic volvulus and pseudo intestinal obstruction, as well as a reduction in the therapeutic effect of anti-PD drugs due to absorption issues.

pmc-10668741.title: Safety Evaluation of an Intranasally Applied Cocktail of Lactococcus lactis Strains in Pigs
pmc-10668741.creator: Ruth Rattigan, Lukasz Wajda, Abel A. Vlasblom, Alan Wolfe, Aldert L. Zomer, Birgitta Duim, Jaap A. Wagenaar, Peadar G. Lawlor
pmc-10668741.description: Simple SummaryIn this study, the safety of an intranasally applied cocktail of Lactococcus lactis was evaluated in new-born pigs. Prior to farrowing, twelve sows were assigned to either a placebo or cocktail group. Immediately after farrowing, either the placebo or cocktail was applied to both nostrils of all piglets in the corresponding group.

pmc-11466731.title: Complete genome sequence of Treponema pedis GNW45 isolated from dairy cattle with active bovine digital dermatitis in Korea
pmc-11466731.creator: Hector Espiritu, Lovelia Mamuad, Edeneil Jerome Valete, Sang-Suk Lee, Yong-Il Cho
pmc-11466731.description: Treponema pedis, a fastidious anaerobic spirochete, is one of the main pathogens involved in the development and progression of bovine digital dermatitis (BDD), a lameness-causing hoof infection in cattle. Here, the complete genome sequencing of T. pedis GNW45 isolated from a dairy cow infected with BDD, was presented.

pmc-11487491.title: Intersectional analysis of social determinants of health and their association with mortality in patients with multimorbidity
pmc-11487491.creator: Aida Moreno-Juste, Clara Laguna-Berna, Beatriz Poblador-Plou, Amaia Calderón-Larrañaga, Julián Librero, Cristina Lozano-Hernández, Alejandro Santos-Mejías, Marcos Castillo-Jimena, Antonio Gimeno-Miguel, Luis A Gimeno-Feliú
pmc-11487491.description: major global challenge for health systems and daily clinical practice, as well as for epidemiological research [1,2]. Recent evidence has highlighted the limitations of current health care systems for addressing the complex needs of patients with multimorbidity due to inadequate or absent attention to coexisting chronic conditions and failure to perform a comprehensive approach to their care [1,3].

pmc-11639795.title: In Silico Design of Peptide Inhibitors Targeting HER2 for Lung Cancer Therapy
pmc-11639795.creator: Heba Ahmed Alkhatabi, Hisham N. Alatyb
pmc-11639795.description: Simple SummaryHuman epidermal growth factor receptor 2, a protein found on cell surfaces, is often overproduced in aggressive forms of cancers like breast, gastric, ovarian, and lung cancers. This overproduction can lead to rapid tumor growth and poor patient outcomes. Current treatments target this protein to slow cancer progression, but more effective and precise options are needed.

pmc-11709658.title: Novel mechanisms of cytosolic phospholipase A2 beta in neurodegeneration and cognitive impairments of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11709658.creator: Qiulan Ma, Brandon Ebright, Jing Li, Dante Dikeman, Ashley Sanchez, Jasmin Galvan, Daniel Badie, Boyang Li, Shaowei Wang, Bilal Ersen Kerman, Debra Hawes, Kyle Hurth, David A. Bennett, Zoe Arvanitakis, Stan G Louie, Hussein N Yassine
pmc-11709658.description: BackgroundSynaptic loss predicts cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the critical disease modifying molecular mechanisms of synaptic failure remain elusive. Animal studies implicate the increased activation of cytosolic phospholipase (cPLA2) activation in synaptic loss and neuroinflammation. cPLA2 activation in human brain synapses have not yet been demonstrated.

pmc-12872562.title: Mechanism of exercise-derived circulating exosomes as a target for sarcopenia management
pmc-12872562.creator: Xiangbo Wang, Hui Huang, Jie Chen, Qing Zhang, Zhichao Yuan, Mingyue Yin, Chenggen Peng, Songlin Liu
pmc-12872562.description: Sarcopenia, an age-related syndrome characterized by the progressive decline of skeletal muscle mass and function, threatens the health of older adults through underlying mechanisms that include dysregulated protein metabolism, autophagy-mitochondrial dysfunction, chronic inflammation, and impaired regenerative capacity of muscle stem cells. Exercise-derived circulating exosomes, which act as key mediators of intercellular communication, show considerable potential in mitigating sarcopenia-related damage.

pmc-12968427.title: Increased Urinary Extracellular Vesicles and Reduced Expression of NEDD4L in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Diabetic Nephropathy
pmc-12968427.creator: Nikhil Thyagarajan, Richard Le Leu, Sharad Kumar, Shilpanjali Jesudason, Jantina A Manning, Marco Infante
pmc-12968427.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionDiabetic nephropathy (DN) is a leading cause of chronic kidney disease. Current diagnosis requires the persistent presence of albuminuria and/or reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate, often detected only at late stages of disease. In recent years, extracellular vesicles (EVs), lipid bilayer membrane–enclosed particles that shed from cells, have gained momentum as a potential source of biomarkers for DN, reflecting pathological changes in this condition.

pmc-12971836.title: Dexamethasone therapy in adolescents with inadequately controlled congenital adrenal hyperplasia: effects on hormonal Suppression, Puberty, and gonadal outcomes
pmc-12971836.creator: N Berna Çelik Ertaş, Burcu Şenkalfa, Doğuş Vurallı, Z Alev Özön, E Nazlı Gönç
pmc-12971836.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposePuberty poses challenges for the management of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH) due to changes in the endocrine milieu and non-compliance with treatment. Uncontrolled hyperandrogenemia is a significant problem, especially for CAH patients in this age group. Along with the attainment of final height, a therapeutic window emerges for employing more potent glucocorticoids (GCs) to improve disease management in the pediatric age group. Dexamethasone (Dex) is a long-acting and more potent GC, and offers a convenient dosing schedule for patients.

pmc-13093975.title: Farnesyltransferase inhibitor LB42708 disables oncogenic RAS signaling and overcomes gefitinib resistance in NSCLC via FTase α-subunit and RAS degradation
pmc-13093975.creator: Guancong Luo, Dexuan Li, Jun Peng, Rongsheng Liu, Yajing Meng, Richard Ward, Yangyang Zhang, Xinyu Zhang, Fengxian Cui, Jiwei Wang, Xiuyu Yang, Mo Chen, Yanjun Xu, Sheng Chen, Wenyu Jiang, Le Zhang, Yurong Li, Yang Yang, Cheng Xiang, Xiaoxi Guo, Jiameng Dai, Jun Sang, Tian-Rui Xu, Su An
pmc-13093975.description: RAS mutations are among the most common oncogenic drivers in human cancers, particularly in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Direct targeting of RAS proteins remains difficult due to the lack of suitable drug-binding pockets on their surfaces. LB42708 is a potent and selective farnesyltransferase (FTase) inhibitor that disrupts RAS farnesylation and downstream signaling.

pmc-13233621.title: Deforestation-induced drying lowers Amazon climate threshold
pmc-13233621.creator: Nico Wunderling, Boris Sakschewski, Johan Rockström, Bernardo M Flores, Marina Hirota, Arie Staal
pmc-13233621.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Humanity is putting unprecedented pressures on the Amazon forest system through global warming and land use changes1,2. As the Amazon forest may undergo self-reinforcing transitions, these pressures could lead to system-wide changes across major parts of Amazonian ecosystems1–4. Here we apply a dynamical systems model to assess the local and far-reaching cascading transition risks towards degraded ecosystems in the Amazon biome under different Shared Socioeconomic Pathways.

pmc-13322219.title: Established and Emerging Less Invasive Biomarkers and Technologies for Lung Cancer Screening: Puerto Rican Context
pmc-13322219.creator: Keisy Rodriguez-Villafañe, Clara Santiago, Juan E. Figueroa, Edwin Figueroa, Yamixa Delgado
pmc-13322219.description: Background/Objectives:In Puerto Rico (PR), lung cancer mortality remains high because diagnoses frequently occur at advanced stages. Although low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) lowers lung cancer–specific mortality, this screening is difficult to operationalize locally due to high false-positive rates, radiology capacity constraints, payer limitations, and geographic barriers affecting rural populations.

pmc-13378335.title: Affective memories of school physical education, life-phase timing of formative experiences, and adult sport and exercise participation: a quota-representative study in Germany
pmc-13378335.creator: Ralf Brand, Reinhold Kliegl
pmc-13378335.description: BackgroundSchool physical education (PE) is one of the few contexts in which nearly all individuals encounter structured movement. We explored whether adults’ PE memories relate to sport and exercise participation across behavioral dimensions such as engagement, time investment, and participation style.

pmc-13538171.title: Teriparatide treatment of osteoporosis in solid organ transplant recipients—a single-center experience
pmc-13538171.creator: Talia Diker Cohen, Ilana Shraga-Slutzky, Keren Kaminer, Alexander Gorshtein, Idit Dotan, Gloria Tsvetov
pmc-13538171.description: SummarySolid organ transplant recipients face high fracture risk with limited evidence guiding anabolic therapy. In this real-world cohort, teriparatide was associated with significant improvements in bone mineral density and acceptable safety without adverse graft effects. These findings support selective anabolic treatment in high-risk transplant recipients and highlight the need for prospective studies.
